patterns.usage_note: The hearsay そうだ repeats a report as received, with no hedging and no evidence of the speaker's own, and it attaches to plain forms (降ったそうだ, いいそうだ, 学生だそうだ). Keep it clear of the look-alike conjecture そうだ, which attaches to the masu-stem or adjective stem (降りそうだ, いい→よさそうだ) and inflects like a な-adjective; the hearsay form has essentially only 〜そうだ／〜そうで, with no prenominal 〜そうな and no negative of its own. Naming the source with 〜によると is common.

examples.ruby: 北[きた]の山[やま]では、ゆうべ初雪[はつゆき]が降[ふ]ったそうだ。
examples.english: They say the first snow of the year fell in the northern mountains last night.

examples.ruby: あの旅館[りょかん]の朝食[ちょうしょく]はとても評判[ひょうばん]がいいそうです。
examples.english: I hear that inn's breakfast has quite a reputation.

examples.ruby: 新[あたら]しい市長[しちょう]は来月[らいげつ]、庁舎[ちょうしゃ]を建[た]て替[か]えるそうだ。
examples.english: The new mayor is reportedly going to rebuild city hall next month.
